summary: Appointed H. A. Gudger Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of the Canal Zone at $6,500 a year, effective January 4, 1909.
Named Wesley M. Owen an Associate Justice of the Supreme Court of the Canal Zone at $6,000 a year, effective January 4, 1909.
Waived the six-month service requirement so W. W. Adams could transfer from the postal service to deputy collector of internal revenue once he passed an examination.

Consented to limit China's Boxer indemnity bond payments to $13,655,492.69 plus 4 percent interest, remitting the rest of the U.S. share "as an act of friendship" under a May 1908 joint resolution of Congress.
Returned to the public domain unallotted lands in New Mexico that 1907 and 1908 orders had added to the Navajo Reservation, except for 110 unapproved allotments described in the order.
Allowed C. M. Huntington to sit for a civil-service examination despite rule provisions that would have disqualified him.
Extended federal railroad safety-appliance laws to the Canal Zone, requiring automatic couplers, brakes, hand holds and other trainmen protections on carriers there, including the Panama Railroad.
Set rules for sailors and Marines riding Army transports, and soldiers aboard naval vessels: each follows the ship's regulations and shares police and guard duty when the commanding officer directs.
Amended civil-service Rule X so anyone who had served at least two years in the office of the President could transfer to a competitive classified position after tests of fitness.
Permitted Grace W. Nettleton, ranked on Connecticut's clerk registers, to be appointed to a clerkship in the Treasury Department.
Let Fannie C. Chase return as a skilled laborer at the Government Printing Office without regard to the civil-service time limit on reinstatement.
Revoked Executive Order 632½ of May 10, 1907, and directed that the vessel Zafiro be transferred back from the Secretary of War to the Secretary of the Navy.
Placed five and three-quarter acres of the Honolulu naval reservation on Kaakaukukui Reef under the Secretary of War to protect the harbor's submarine-mine defenses.
Moved the land office at Mitchell, South Dakota, to Gregory and transferred certain described lands out of the Chamberlain land district.
Created a Council of the Fine Arts, calling the attention of executive department heads to the President's correspondence with the American Institute of Architects on the subject.
Added timbered lands in Nevada to the Humboldt National Forest, formed the year before from the Ruby Mountains and Independence forests.
Enlarged the Moapa National Forest in Nevada, the 1908 merger of the Charleston and Vegas forests, by adding partly timbered public lands.
Canceled a 1908 order turning Fort Keogh, Montana, over to the Interior Department, and placed the military reservation's lands back under the War Department for military use.
Allowed William H. Baldwin to stay on as a special examiner in the Bureau of Corporations for as long as the Department of Commerce and Labor needed him.
Reserved certain described lands in Minnesota for lighthouse purposes.
Redrew the Cleveland National Forest in Southern California, adding partly timbered lands and cutting out others, which returned to the public domain.
Enlarged Florida's Pelican Island Reservation to take in unreserved mangrove and other islands nearby, keeping the ban on hunting birds or taking their eggs there.
Permitted Edwin W. Hutcheson to be reinstated in the classified service in any department, once he passed an appropriate examination.
Expanded the Pecos National Forest in the Territory of New Mexico with additional partly timbered public lands.
Allowed Edward C. Baker, a former vice-consul in China, to be appointed a class 3 clerk in the State Department for his special knowledge of Far East affairs.
Reinstated Daniel F. Dolan as a post-office inspector, with a sixty-day suspension starting on the date of his return.
Grew the Prescott National Forest in Arizona Territory, recently merged with the Verde forest, by adding partly timbered lands.
Excepted national-bank examiners and receivers under the Comptroller of the Currency from civil-service examination.
Set aside a chain of islets and reefs at the far western end of the Hawaiian Archipelago, from Cure Island to Necker Island, as the Hawaiian Islands Reservation for native birds.
Reserved certain described lands in Minnesota for lighthouse purposes.
Set aside certain described lands on Michigan Island, Wisconsin, for lighthouse purposes.
Extended the deadline for the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission to finish its work to September 2, 1909.
Reserved lands near Rampart, Alaska, for a Department of Agriculture experiment station.
Added partly timbered lands and undergrowth in Arizona Territory to the Tonto National Forest.
Created the Marquette National Forest from partly timbered public lands in Michigan, reserving them from settlement or entry.
Established the Nevada National Forest, setting apart partly timbered public lands in the state for the use and benefit of the people.
Enlarged the Dixie National Forest with partly timbered lands in Utah.
Allowed Charles B. Brewer to return as a ship draftsman in the Navy's Bureau of Construction and Repair regardless of how long he had been out of service.
Permitted James J. Smith's promotion from night inspector to day inspector in the Customs Service at the port of New York.
Set apart partly timbered public lands in Michigan as the Michigan National Forest, closed to settlement or entry.
Declared February 12, 1909, the 100th anniversary of Abraham Lincoln's birth, a special legal holiday in the District of Columbia and the territories, as a joint resolution of Congress directed.
Extended the Klamath National Forest in California with additional partly timbered lands.
Created the Superior National Forest in Minnesota, reserving partly timbered public lands from settlement or entry for the use and benefit of the people.
Reserved lands north of the Olongapo naval reservation on Subic Bay in the Philippines for naval purposes, extending its boundaries under the Secretary of the Navy.
Changed the Gila National Forest's boundaries in New Mexico Territory, adding partly timbered lands and releasing others back to the public domain.
Revised the Black Hills National Forest, whose Wyoming portion had gone to the Sundance forest in 1908, by adding partly timbered lands in South Dakota.
Enlarged the Sioux National Forest, a 1908 merger of five Montana and South Dakota forests, with more partly timbered lands in South Dakota.
Expanded the Tongass National Forest in southeast Alaska, redrawing its bounds from the Skagway River along the Canadian boundary to Cape Muzon.
Created a sixth internal revenue district in California by taking counties out of the first district.
Allowed R. Barnard Talcott to be reinstated as assistant chief mechanical and electrical engineer in the Supervising Architect's office without meeting civil-service rules.
Waived promotion rules so John Hunter, Peter J. Kaster and Joseph Stangle could move from laborer to assistant weigher in the Customs Service at the port of New York.
Added partly timbered Nevada lands to the Toiyabe National Forest, consolidated in 1908 with the Monitor and Toquima forests.
Extended the 1906 commercial agreement with Spain to sparkling wines, setting reduced U.S. duties on Spanish sparkling wine in exchange for Spanish concessions on American goods.
Combined the Datil and Magdalena National Forests, plus unreserved timbered lands in New Mexico Territory, into a single forest named the Datil National Forest.
Enlarged Alaska's Chugach National Forest, taking in Afognak Island and the former Afognak Forest and Fish Culture Reserve plus public lands around the Copper River and Kenai Mountains.
Reserved lands along the Copper and Klutina Rivers in Alaska for joint educational and agricultural experiment purposes.
Added partly timbered California lands to the Modoc National Forest, merged in 1908 with the Warner Mountains forest.
Enlarged the Ozark National Forest in Arkansas with additional partly timbered lands.
Expanded the California National Forest, formed in 1908 from parts of the Stony Creek and Trinity forests, with more partly timbered lands.
Allowed F. N. Clark to be hired as a clerk at the Interstate Commerce Commission without regard to civil-service rules.
Turned seventeen Reclamation Service reservoir sites in ten western states and territories, from Salt River, Arizona, to Pathfinder, Wyoming, into preserves and breeding grounds for native birds.
Made ten Spanish Treaty Claims Commission employees commended by its president eligible for transfer to the competitive service after noncompetitive examination.
Called the U.S. Senate into special session at noon on March 4, 1909, to receive communications from the Executive.
Added more partly timbered lands in Arkansas to the Arkansas National Forest.
Made five employees of the Assistant Attorney-General's office defending Spanish Treaty Claims suits eligible for transfer to the competitive service after noncompetitive examination.
Let Roger H. Adams, a clerk in the Isthmian service, transfer to a competitive position in the United States, subject to examination.
Reserved three town blocks in Nome, Alaska, for an Army Signal Corps wireless telegraph station tied to the territory's telegraph lines.
Reserved Saint Matthew Island, Hall Island and Pinnacle Islet in the Bering Sea as the Bering Sea Reservation, a preserve and breeding ground for native birds.
Set aside Fire Island, near the head of Cook Inlet, Alaska, as a preserve and breeding ground for the Alaska moose.
Protected Chisick Island and Egg Island at the entrance to Tuxedni Harbor, Cook Inlet, as the Tuxedni Reservation for native birds, outlawing hunting or egg-taking there.
Made Saint Lazaria Island, at the entrance to Sitka Sound, a preserve and breeding ground for native birds.
Reserved the treeless tundra of the Yukon River delta in Alaska as the Yukon Delta Reservation, a preserve and breeding ground for native birds.
Set apart the islands of the Culebra group in Puerto Rico, except Culebra Island itself, as a native-bird preserve, subject to existing naval and lighthouse uses.
Reserved the Middle and North Farallon islands and nearby rocks off California as the Farallon Reservation, a preserve and breeding ground for native birds.
Protected Walrus and Otter islands in Alaska's Pribilof group as a native-bird preserve, subject to existing law on fur-bearing animals.
Added partly timbered lands in California and Nevada to the Mono National Forest.
Brought timbered parts of the White Mountain Apache Indian Reservation into Arizona's Sitgreaves National Forest, with provisos covering allotments to Indians and grazing use.
Enlarged the Lincoln National Forest, merged in 1908 with the Gallinas forest, by adding partly timbered lands in New Mexico Territory.
Expanded the Shasta National Forest with partly timbered California lands, including part of the area formerly in the Lassen National Forest.
Added timbered parts of the Mescalero Apache Indian Reservation to the Alamo National Forest in New Mexico Territory, with provisos for continued use for the Indians.
Enlarged the Carson National Forest with unreserved lands and part of the Jicarilla Apache Indian Reservation, with provisos for continued use for the Indians.
Took public lands, including parts of the Zuni and Navajo Indian Reservations, into the Zuni National Forest, keeping for 25 years the government's right to allot those lands to individual Indians.
Added timbered parts of the Hoopa Valley Indian Reservation in California to the Trinity National Forest, with provisos for continued use for the Indians.
Enlarged Arizona's Apache National Forest with timbered lands from the White Mountain Apache Indian Reservation, with provisos for continued use for the Indians.
Redrew the Lassen National Forest, shifting part of it to the Shasta National Forest and adding other partly timbered California lands.
Added partly timbered lands in California to the Plumas National Forest.

Created Mount Olympus National Monument in Washington's Olympic Mountains to protect its glaciers and the summer range and breeding grounds of the Olympic elk, a species "rapidly decreasing in numbers."
Extended the Tahoe National Forest with partly timbered lands in California and Nevada.
Brought timbered parts of the Tule River Indian Reservation into California's Sequoia National Forest, with provisos for continued use for the Indians.
Allowed James Mullenbach to be appointed, without examination, as the Immigration Service inspector in charge of information and distribution work in Chicago, given his particular qualifications.
Narrowed the civil-service exception in U.S. marshals' offices to field deputies and those whose chief duty is serving process, bringing other deputies into the competitive service.
Permitted John M. Longan of Massachusetts to be appointed to a clerical position in the classified service without meeting civil-service requirements.
Excused federal employees in the District of Columbia from work on Inauguration Day.
Made the volcanic Bogoslof islands in Alaska's Aleutian chain a preserve and breeding ground for native birds, named the Bogoslof Reservation.
Made six Justice Department employees, paid from the antitrust enforcement and Five Civilized Tribes appropriations, eligible for transfer to the competitive service after noncompetitive examination.
